'''2000 Decipher World Championship''' was the fifth Star Wars CCG World Championship, played 5–7 October 2000 at [[DecipherCon 2000]] in the Doubletree Resort and Conference Center, Kissimmee, Florida. [[Matt Sokol]] (United States) defeated [[Yannick Lapointe]] (Canada) in the Final Confrontation.<ref name="wp">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia</ref><ref name="sokol">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041026224145/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv16.htm Matt Sokol interview], [[Trandosite]] (25 October 2000)</ref><ref name="sched">[https://web.archive.org/web/20061009205800/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/schedule/ DecipherCon 2000 schedule], Decipher (Wayback 9 October 2006)</ref>

[[File:DecipherCon 2000 SWCCG champion plaque.jpg|thumb|right|280px|2000 World Champion plaque]]
[[File:DecipherCon 2000 tournament hall.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Main hall during the convention, 6 October 2000]]

The constructed pool was [[Premiere - Death Star II]]. Wikipedia and ''Star Wars Insider'' 52 list 72 Day 1 players. Francis K. Lalumiere, writing from the floor on 5 October, put 170 competitors in the main hall for Day 1. Sokol was player 36 on Day 1. He lost the first final game and won the second; combined score 2 (+5) to 2 (−5).<ref name="sokol" /><ref name="wp" /><ref name="insider">''Star Wars Insider'' 52 (2000)</ref><ref name="fkl2">[https://web.archive.org/web/20010107221700/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/fkl2.html Mighty Jabba Sails Across the Atlantic], Francis K. Lalumiere, Decipher (Wayback 7 January 2001)</ref><ref name="jls3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20001117011300/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/jls3.html Matt Sokol, 2000 Star Wars CCG World Champion!], Jean-Luc Simard, Decipher (Wayback 17 November 2000)</ref>

== Format ==

* '''Environment:''' [[Premiere - Death Star II]]
* '''Site:''' [[DecipherCon 2000]], Doubletree Resort and Conference Center, Kissimmee, Florida
* '''Dates:''' 5–7 October 2000 (Thursday–Saturday); the convention continued through 8 October
* '''Field:''' 72 Day 1 (Wikipedia / ''Insider'' 52); 58 Day 2 (Decipher results page)<ref name="wp" /><ref name="d2">[https://web.archive.org/web/20001026043505/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/results/starwars.html DecipherCon 2000 Day 2]</ref><ref name="insider" />

Day 2 was eight games (4 Light / 4 Dark). Twelve advanced to Day 3. Day 3 reset those twelve for four games (2 Light / 2 Dark); top two played the Final Confrontation.<ref name="d3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20010303120030/http://decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/results/starwars3.html DecipherCon 2000 Day 3]</ref>

The last Day 2 slot was [[Dominic Gaudreault]] 10 (+70). [[Martin Akesson]] 10 (+69) missed by one differential. On Day 3, [[Kevin Shannon]]'s Game 2 Dark vs [[Steve Brentson]] was a '''Modified Win by 14''' (+1 victory point). A full win there would have moved Shannon past Sokol on the cut math; that example is on [[Tournaments#2000 World Championship — Sokol, Shannon, and a modified win]].<ref name="d3" />

== Final Confrontation ==

The match was played in a closed room. The audience watched on a large screen next door, with commentary by [[Joe Alread]], [[Kyle Heuer]], and Kendrick Summers. Jean-Luc Simard's Decipher report and Sokol's Decktech report are the play-by-play sources.<ref name="jls3" /><ref name="sokol-dt">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-sokols-dcon-2000-reportd1327/ sokols-dcon-2000-report], Matt Sokol, Decktech (11 October 2000)</ref>

Game 1: Sokol [[Hidden Base]] (X-wings / Numbers) against Lapointe [[Bring Him Before Me]]. Sokol's Light list went in at 59 cards; he added [[Civil Disorder]] at registration and the deck had no Luke. Lapointe won by 20.<ref name="jls3" /><ref name="sokol-dt" />

Game 2: Sokol [[ISB Operations]] (walkers / Sandwhirl) against Lapointe's Super Falcon list. Sokol needed at least 21 Force of differential. An [[Abyssin Ornament]] left him on 25 Life Force; Lapointe drew his last card. Combined: Sokol 2 (+5), Lapointe 2 (−5).<ref name="jls3" />

Team Albany built the ISB list overnight after Day 2. Sokol later won the Sunday team constructed event with that group.<ref name="sokol-dt" /><ref name="sokol" />

The Player's Council posted the original Decipher streaming video of both games:

[[File:DecipherCon 2000 Worlds Final still.jpg|640px|link=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk]]

[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk Watch the Final Confrontation] (1 hour 21 minutes). Convention, guests, side events, and the surviving official photographs are on [[DecipherCon 2000]].
